title: Site comparison preserves and detects Tor intervals
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, and let $K\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{Et}},A)$ in the ordinary derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Use the full small pro-etale site and its ordinary derived category $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and the comparison inverse image $\nu_T^*$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], applied termwise on derived categories [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. For integers $a\leq b$, $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude] if and only if $\nu_T^*K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Thus the test is against every module sheaf on the respective site, with no constructibility or etale-origin restriction on the pro-etale test sheaves.

proof.text: Put $F=\nu_T^*$. By [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level], $F$ is exact and every module sheaf $M$ has $M\cong\nu_{T,*}FM$. Consequently $FM=0$ implies $M=0$. Part (3) of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] gives $\mathcal H^i(FC)\cong F\mathcal H^i(C)$ for every complex $C$ and integer $i$. The derived functor here is termwise $F$ by [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Hence vanishing of each cohomology sheaf is preserved and reflected; there is no boundedness restriction in this calculation.

source.place: Tag 099T, lemma-fully-faithful; Tag 099V, lemma-relative-comparison (termwise inverse image); elementary kernel/image argument

proof.text: Assume that $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Choose a representing complex $C$ and a K-flat resolution $R\to C$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By the formula in [def-kun-derived-tensor], $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_T[0]$ is represented by $R\otimes_A A_T[0]\cong R$, so $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. Replace $C$ by its upper smart truncation: retain $C^i$ for $i<b$, use $\ker(d^b)$ in degree $b$, and zero above $b$. The inclusion is a quasi-isomorphism since $\mathcal H^i(C)=0$ for $i>b$. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement] to this complex, with $N=b$, obtaining a quasi-isomorphism $P\to\tau_{\leq b}C$ with flat terms and $P^i=0$ for $i>b$. By [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site], $P$ is K-flat, so $P\otimes_A N$ computes $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N$ for every etale module sheaf $N$.

source.place: Tags 08FZ (definition-tor-amplitude), 08G1 (lemma-tor-amplitude), 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat); upper smart truncation written out

proof.text: For every etale module sheaf $N$, the Tor bound gives $\mathcal H^{a-1}(P\otimes_A N)=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-opcycles-tor-criterion] on the etale site with $\mathcal O=A_T$ and $n=a$ to conclude that $Q=P^a/\operatorname{im}(d^{a-1})$ is flat. Form $B$ with $B^a=Q$, $B^i=P^i$ for $a<i\leq b$, and zero otherwise, with the induced differentials. The projection $P\to B$ induces an isomorphism on cohomology in degrees $i\geq a$ by the kernel/image formulas, and both sides have zero cohomology below $a$ because $P$ represents $K$. Thus $B$ represents $K$ and is a flat complex supported precisely within $[a,b]$.

source.place: Tag 08G0, lemma-last-one-flat; Tag 08G1, lemma-tor-amplitude, lower smart truncation; existing universal-tensor opcycle criterion specialized at n=a

proof.text: By [lem-exc-constant-inverse-image-flat] every term of $FB$ is flat, and by exactness [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] the termwise pullback of the quasi-isomorphism just constructed is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus $FB$ represents $\nu_T^*K$ by [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. It is zero outside $[a,b]$, and is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] on the full small pro-etale site. For an arbitrary pro-etale $A_T$-module sheaf $M$, [def-weil-derived-tensor] therefore computes $\nu_T^*K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M$ by $FB\otimes_A M$. This complex has zero terms outside $[a,b]$, so its cohomology vanishes there. This proves the forward implication, with all test sheaves allowed as required by [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude].

source.place: First paragraph: pull back the bounded flat model; K-flat computation justified by Stacks Tags 06YQ and 06YU

proof.text:
Part (1) of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] identifies $\nu_T^{-1}A_{T,\mathrm{Et}}\cong A_{T,\mathrm{proet}}$ as ring sheaves and identifies ringed module pullback with $F$. Exactness then identifies $LF$ with termwise $F$: the augmentation from a K-flat resolution is a quasi-isomorphism after $F$, so it becomes an isomorphism in the derived category. This is the unbounded derived functor of [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to this constant-coefficient ringed comparison morphism to obtain, for every etale module sheaf $N$, a canonical isomorphism
$$F(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N)\cong FK\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}FN.$$
The site-size hypotheses of that lemma hold by choosing the skeletons in the common larger universe specified in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. In particular, $FN$ is an ordinary pro-etale module sheaf in degree zero. No boundedness of $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N$ is needed: the cited tensor theorem holds on unbounded derived categories.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; Tag 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat; constant-ring specialization of the comparison geometric morphism

proof.text:
Conversely assume $FK$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. For any etale module sheaf $N$, its inverse image $FN$ is a pro-etale module sheaf placed in degree zero. The isomorphism of step 5 gives, for $i\notin[a,b]$,
$$F\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N)\cong\mathcal H^i(FK\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}FN)=0.$$
Here the first identification uses the kernel/image calculation of step 1. The sheaf unit isomorphism of [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] then gives $\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N)=0$. Since $N$ was arbitrary, this is exactly the etale Tor-amplitude condition [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Together with step 4 it proves the equivalence.

lean.statement: theorem comparison_torAmplitudeIn_iff (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A] (T : Scheme.{u}) (a b : ℤ) (_hab : a ≤ b) (K : _root_.DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} A)))) : Etale.DerivedCategory.hasTorAmplitudeIn (ULift.{u + 1, u} A) T a b K.obj ↔ Scheme.HasProEtaleTorAmplitude T A ((finiteCoefficientIntrinsicRealization T A).mapDerivedCategory.obj ((siteComparisonDerivedPullbackPlus T (ULift.{u + 1, u} A)).obj K).obj) a b
lean.note: Second reading: use the recorded etale hasTorAmplitudeIn and intrinsic HasProEtaleTorAmplitude, with canonical finiteCoefficientIntrinsicRealization after the recorded siteComparisonDerivedPullbackPlus.
